title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 300
text:
61. Religious, social or cultural reasons are sometimes given for FGM. However, FGM is child
abuse, and since 2003 it has been a criminal offence in the UK (Female Genital Mutilation
Act 2003).

62. There are no medical reasons to carry out FGM. It does not enhance fertility, and it does not
make childbirth safer. It is used to control female sexuality and can cause severe and
long-lasting damage to physical and emotional health.
239

63. H ealth and social care professionals and teachers have been required since 2015 to report
“known” cases of FGM.240 These professionals are required to make a report to the police if,
in the course of their professional duties, they:
• Are informed by a girl under 18 that an act of FGM has been carried out on her.
• Observe physical signs which appear to show that an act of FGM has been carried out on
a girl under 18 and have no reason to believe that the act was necessary for the girl’s
physical or mental health or for purposes connected with labour or birth.
